decisions.statement: An argument a change was handed no value for is refused by the key naming that argument.
An argument a change does not take is refused by the key naming it.
That refusal names every argument the change does take.
That refusal points at the argument nearest the key, where one is near enough.
An edit states whether the readers of its path owe the reading again.
An edit stating nothing there leaves its readers owing the reading.
Edits gather by joining the edits in the order the edits were stated.
Gathering reconciles nothing.
A move landing where another edit already answers is refused.
One refusal refuses the whole answer.
An edit holds only what making that edit takes.
An add has a path and the content that path is to hold.
An append has a path and the content that path is to end with.
A replace has a path and the passage each side.
A remove has a path alone.
A move has the path moved from and the path moved to.
A bring has a path alone.
The body a bring leaves is the body its path already holds.
A bring names no body, so a body of any bytes goes through a bring.
A bring at a path holding no body is refused.
The path an edit leaves a body at is the path moved to for a move and the path named otherwise.
A whole body written over another is a replace with the whole body each side.
A splice has the place a body changes and the content that place is to hold.
A splice becomes a replace naming the whole lines that place sits in.
A run of lines the body has twice widens a line each side until the run is held once.
A splice widens to the whole body where no run of lines around that splice is held once.
A splice leaving its place as the place was answers no edit.
Many splices are read in the order the splices sit in the body.
Two splices whose lines meet or overlap answer one edit over those lines.
Two splices opening at one place and replacing nothing are joined in the order handed in.
Of two splices opening at one place, one replacing characters is dropped rather than joined.
Two splices whose lines are apart answer two edits.
The body such an edit is worked out from is read off the tree.
Such an edit is worked out against the bodies the earlier edits left.
A path with no characters has no body.
A body that is not text is answered as not text rather than read as characters.
A move and a remove read whether a path holds a body rather than that body.
A passage worked in a body that is not text is refused.
An add onto a path with a body is refused.
An append leaves the body its path holds and puts its content after that body.
An append onto a path with no body leaves that content alone.
An append of no characters is refused.
An append onto a body that is not text is refused.
A move onto a path with a body is refused.
A replace naming a passage its path has twice is refused.
A replace naming a passage of no characters is refused.
An edit leaving the body unchanged narrows to no edit.
Nothing here reads the disk or writes to the disk.

definition: the edits a change answers rather than writes
